Tim H.: hitting a weird TS + ESM problem on edge builds, need help
Tim H.: our SDK types start failing when users import with `import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'` in an edge runtime (bun/deno/next-edge). Errors like: "Generic type inference failed" and overloads not matching.
Tim H.: minimal repro attached (not here) — seems related to package exports + .d.ts generation + tsconfig moduleResolution
Maria L.: can you paste package.json exports & tsconfig? quick guess: conditional exports + type: "module" mismatch is common
Tim H.: sure, here's the relevant bits:
```json
"type": "module",
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
},
"types": "dist/types/index.d.ts"
```
and tsconfig: 
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "declaration": true,
    "declarationMap": true,
    "emitDeclarationOnly": true,
    "stripInternal": false,
    "skipLibCheck": true
  }
}
```
Priya S.: two things to check: 1) are you generating a single flattened index.d.ts that uses `export default`? ESM + `export default` in d.ts vs `export =` for CJS can confuse TS inference. 2) edge bundlers sometimes rewrite imports and change how TS picks up types (moduleResolution)
Priya S.: small workaround we've used: ship both `index.d.ts` for ESM and a `index.cjs.d.ts` and point conditional types in package.json to them. pain but works.
Ashley K.: another common problem: overloads + `unknown` vs `any` — if your call signatures use `unknown` and then you have overloads that rely on infer, TS sometimes picks the wrong overload in consumer code depending on `esModuleInterop`/`allowSyntheticDefaultImports` flags.
Tim H.: interesting — our core call has overloads for `createClient<T>` and `createClient(options, handlers)` and the generic inference seems to prefer the second overload in some setups.
Maria L.: can you show the type snippet?
Tim H.: simplified:
```ts
export default function createClient<T = any>(opts: ClientOpts): Client<T>;
export default function createClient<T = any>(opts: ClientOpts, hooks: Hooks<T>): Client<T>;
```
Tim H.: when imported as `import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'` TS complains second signature incompatible because it can't reconcile default import shape with conditional exports.
Priya S.: try switching to named exports for the factory (export function createClient...) — named exports are much more robust across CJS/ESM boundaries for typings. consumers can still `import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'` if you export a default that delegates to the named function, but types resolve better with named exports.
Ashley K.: also try changing generic defaults to `T extends Record<string, unknown> = Record<string, unknown>` — sometimes `any` loosens overload resolution in surprising ways. using `unknown` with constraints helps inference pick the right signature.
Tim H.: example adjustment suggested?
Maria L.: quick tweak:
```ts
export function createClient<T extends object = {}>(opts: ClientOpts): Client<T>;
export function createClient<T extends object = {}>(opts: ClientOpts, hooks: Hooks<T>): Client<T>;
export default createClient;
```
Maria L.: and ensure your `index.d.ts` doesn't re-export default in a way that TS treats as `typeof import("...").default` vs the named symbol.
Priya S.: for tsconfig, try `moduleResolution: "bundler"` for consumers on modern toolchains, or `node16` / `nodeNext` depending on target. also set `esModuleInterop: true` in examples to help folks on older setups.
Tim H.: ok good tips. any runtime specific for edge? I saw a weird deno error about "Cannot use this import style in edge"
Ashley K.: some edge runtimes have stricter resolver semantics — they prefer pure ESM. If your package exports both CJS and ESM via conditional exports, ensure the ESM entrypoint's types are discoverable (the "types" field in package.json should point to a d.ts that matches the import condition). e.g. use conditional exports for types: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "types": "./dist/types/esm/index.d.ts",
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
  }
}
```
Maria L.: note: Node's conditional `types` field is newer but supported by TS. Make sure to publish those files.
Priya S.: also add a small note in onboarding docs: "If you're on edge runtime X, use `import { createClient } from 'redwood-sdk'` or set tsconfig's `moduleResolution` accordingly" — reduces support tickets.
Tim H.: thanks. putting together a patch: 1) prefer named exports in types, 2) add `types` per conditional export, 3) update example tsconfig in README to recommend `esModuleInterop: true` or `moduleResolution: bundler`.
dev-bot: created issue #1347: "SDK: TS/ESM typing + edge import friction" (assigned to @timh) :robot_face:
Tim H.: assigning myself, will open a minimal repro repo and PR with typed changes + README edits. rough ETA EOD tomorrow.
Maria L.: :+1: lmk if you want me to review the d.ts output — happy to sanity-check the emitted declarations.
Ashley K.: we should also add a short automated test in the SDK repo that builds types with nodeNext and bundler configs and tries consuming them from a tiny TS consumer to catch regressions.
Tim H.: good idea. I'll add CI matrix job. thanks all :)
Maria L.: :rocket:
